metadata.context_note: Stage 1 of feature-pipeline per ADR-0017. Special case: source raw_request was a doc_type:issue-proposal at Issues/issue-capture-mechanism/proposal.md (planning-mode design work). Clarifier surfaced 7 ambiguities as proposed defaults rather than via AskUserQuestion (no tool available); defaults bind at Gate 1 user confirmation. The proposal-as-prior-context handoff pattern is itself the subject of this feature run.

verdict.summary: PASS_WITH_RECOMMENDATIONS — structurally complete; logically consistent; substantively well-grounded in the proposal+plan prior context. Two important findings concern over-reach into PRD-territory authoring (extensive FR/NFR/AC seed lists, 9-layer table at intent stage) and one borderline layer-disposition judgment. None are blockers; all are appropriately framed as 'seed' / 'preliminary' and explicitly accommodate the proposal-as-prior-context pattern. The user may want to confirm at Gate 1 that the seed-list extent is acceptable as Open-Item framing rather than premature requirements authoring.
conditions: User confirms at Gate 1 that the 7 proposed defaults (recorded in 'Clarifying Questions and Answers') are correctly resolved. Per the orchestrator note and the doc's §Confirmation, any rejected default reopens that row before PRD authoring begins.

User confirms at Gate 1 that the extensive 'Open Items (Pending PRD Authoring)' content (FR seeds, NFR seeds, EARS AC seeds, 9-layer table) is acceptable as Open-Item framing inherited from the proposal+plan prior context, rather than premature PRD authoring forbidden by the template's authoring-notes.

PRD author treats Layer 3 (Backend) disposition for the validator-extension as a soft signal — Discovery may reassign to Layer 1 (Claude Code / Project Filesystem) given the script is project-tooling, not a service.

issues.location: §Open Items (Pending PRD Authoring), subsections 'Functional capabilities to formalize as FRs', 'Non-functional concerns to formalize as NFRs', 'Acceptance criteria to formalize in EARS at PRD time', 'Exhaustive 9-layer scope declaration' (lines ~304–403)
issues.description: The Open Items section contains ~12 FR seed bullets, ~8 NFR seed bullets, ~12 EARS-format AC seeds (with full WHEN…SHALL syntax), and a fully-populated 9-layer disposition table. The template's authoring-notes explicitly state that intake-intent-clarifier 'MUST NOT' author Functional Requirements (PRD's job), Acceptance Criteria (PRD/Blueprint's job), or make design decisions (per-layer Design's job). The doc partially mitigates this by framing items as 'seed list' / 'preliminary' / 'the PRD author may renumber / split / combine' and by titling the section 'Pending PRD Authoring'.
issues.evidence_for: Template authoring-notes section in intent-clarification-template.md, lines 117–122: 'What this sub-agent MUST NOT do: Author Functional Requirements (that's the PRD), Author Acceptance Criteria (that's the PRD/Blueprint), Make design decisions (that's per-layer Design)'.
issues.evidence_against: Orchestrator context note explicitly accommodates proposal-as-prior-context pattern; the proposal+companion plan supply substantive pre-decided content; clarifier framed work as 'seed' rather than 'final'; deferring this content forces the PRD author to re-derive from the same proposal.
issues.suggestion: Surface explicitly to user at Gate 1: 'The proposal+plan pre-loaded substantial structural content. The intent-clarifier carried that forward as seeds in Open Items rather than re-elicit. Confirm this framing is acceptable; if not, the PRD author will start from the proposal directly.' If user agrees, this finding becomes wontfix-with-rationale (explicit accommodation). If not, the Open Items subsections should be reduced to bullet-summaries with pointers to the proposal.

issues.location: §Scope Posture > Exhaustive 9-layer scope declaration, Layer 3 row (line ~392)
issues.description: Layer 3 (Backend) is marked 'IN scope (secondary)' on grounds that the validator-script extension at .claude/skills/auditing-shared/scripts/validate_pipeline_frontmatter.py is a 'Python script — tooling/infra logic, not a service, but lives in the backend layer per the taxonomy.' The 9-layer taxonomy defines Backend as 'services, domain logic, background jobs, schedulers' (KB-documentation-criteria layer-taxonomy.md). The validator is a pre-commit / Gate-0 audit utility under .claude/skills/auditing-shared/, which is arguably Layer 1 (Claude Code / Project Filesystem) territory — Layer 1's description includes 'skills, MCP configuration, project conventions'.
issues.suggestion: Flag for PRD/Discovery to confirm: is the validator-script extension a Layer 1 concern (lives under .claude/skills/, project tooling) or a Layer 3 concern (Python codebase logic)? Either is defensible; the call belongs to Discovery+Design Composition. Worst case: the per-layer design fanout invokes design-backend unnecessarily, which is recoverable.

issues.description: Template authoring-notes specify length budget of 60–150 lines; this document is 423 lines. The overage is principally in §Open Items (~120 lines) and §Scope Posture > What's in scope (~55 lines), reflecting the proposal+plan pre-decided content carry-forward.
issues.suggestion: Acceptable in this special-case run (proposal-as-prior-context absorbs ~80% of normal elicitation work into structural carry-forward). For future intent-clarification runs that load a doc_type:issue-proposal, the proposal-as-prior-context template-amendment in scope here should clarify whether this length overshoot is the expected pattern or an outlier. Resolve in the in-scope template edit to intent-clarification-template.md.

issues.location: §Clarifying Questions and Answers, row 3 (validator status vocabulary)
issues.description: Row 3's answer states the plan has 'an internal inconsistency' between a '3-state' cell in the EDIT file-list row and the '5-state' Issue lifecycle section, and resolves to 5-state, calling the 3-state cell 'stale wording to be corrected in Design.' This is a load-bearing decision (the validator's enforcement vocabulary) that propagates to multiple downstream artifacts (templates, validator extension, agent body). The resolution is correct per orchestrator user-instruction context, but the doc should make clear that the 'correction' is itself a Design-stage deliverable (not just plan-comment cleanup).
issues.suggestion: PRD author should ensure the FR list explicitly includes 'Update KB-issue-capture / KB-documentation-criteria source-of-truth language so the 5-state vocabulary is canonical and the 3-state mention is removed' so the plan-comment cleanup doesn't get dropped silently. Already partially captured by FR seed 'Validator extension recognising 3 new doc_type values + 5-state vocabulary' — but make the source-of-truth language cleanup an explicit deliverable, not implicit.

issues.location: §Scope Posture > What's in scope, 'ADR authorship by Design Composition' (line ~187)
issues.description: Lists 7 tentative ADR subjects for Design Composition to author. This is forward-leaning for an intent-clarification (ADRs are Stage-5 deliverables), but the listing is appropriately framed as 'tentative'. The 7 listed subjects mirror the 7 ADR-worthy decisions in the proposal §'Multiple ADR-worthy decisions (none yet ratified)' (lines 50–57 of proposal.md), so the carry-forward is faithful.
issues.suggestion: PRD author and design-composer should treat this list as a hand-off from the proposal — not as authoritative. Final ADR slate is determined at Design Composition. If a subject is later subsumed or split, that's expected and not a regression.

issues.description: user_token: pending-gate1 is a placeholder. Per ADR-0032 Change 2, the gated-artifact frontmatter token chain populates user_token AT Gate confirmation, not pre-Gate. 'pending-gate1' is a reasonable placeholder that signals the value is gate-derived.
issues.suggestion: Orchestrator must replace 'pending-gate1' with the actual confirmation token at Gate 1 acceptance and re-write the frontmatter. Confirm the orchestrator's Gate 1 step includes this frontmatter update — it's mechanical but easy to skip. No change to doc needed pre-Gate.

issues.location: §Clarifying Questions and Answers, row 6 (back-fill status:open and since: on 4 existing files)
issues.description: Row 6's proposed default back-fills status:open and a since: companion field on the 4 existing Issues/*.md files. The original plan-mode design back-fills only version:0.1.0. Adding status:open and since: at this row is the clarifier inferring from the new 5-state vocabulary requirement. The since: companion field's semantics (file's 'earliest known authoring timestamp') is sensible but introduces a new frontmatter field whose definition is not yet specified in any template.
issues.suggestion: PRD author should formalize the since: field semantics in the issue-doctype templates being authored. Confirm at Gate 1 that the user is comfortable with retroactively assigning since: based on git-history first-commit timestamp of each file (or a clarifier-determined fallback if git-blame is ambiguous).

recommendations: User should explicitly confirm at Gate 1: (a) acceptance of the 7 proposed-default resolutions to clarifying questions; (b) acceptance of the Open Items section extent (FR/NFR/AC seeds, 9-layer table) as appropriate carry-forward from the proposal-as-prior-context handoff, rather than premature PRD work.
Orchestrator should update frontmatter user_token from 'pending-gate1' to the confirmation token upon Gate 1 pass.

PRD author should: (1) treat the Open Items seeds as proposal-derived starting points, not finalized requirements; (2) re-check Layer 3 (Backend) disposition for the validator extension — Layer 1 may be the more accurate home; (3) ensure the 5-state-vocabulary canonicalization (per Q3 resolution) is an explicit FR, not just plan-comment cleanup; (4) ensure the since: companion field semantics get formal specification in the new issue-doctype templates.
